summary: Iter 164 — Strict project-based access control for custom 'Manager O P' role verified end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass (test_mop sees exactly 1 project = PRJ-2025-01; cost-centers, project-requests scoped; unassigned-project query returns []; admin sees all; canonical PM regression clean). Frontend: All three targeted dropdowns are scoped correctly for test_mop@erp.com — (a) Project Request Center filter [data-testid=req-filter-project] shows only ['— all projects —', 'PRJ-2025-01 · Reliance Jamnagar Scaffolding']; (b) Cost Centers [data-testid=cc-project-select] shows only PRJ-2025-01; (c) Material Allocations 'Issue' dialog [data-testid=alloc-project] shows only PRJ-2025-01 when Allocate-To=Project is selected. integration_issues.issue: For test_mop@erp.com the top-row create-request buttons (Material Request / Manpower Request / Service | Payment) are NOT rendered — only Refresh, Excel, PDF are shown. Canonical PM sees all three. Per review context note manager_o_p has write on project_requests (backend project_requests_router now allows is_pm_scoped custom roles to raise requests) — this is a frontend RBAC gate mismatch. Backend allows POST /api/project-requests but UI hides the buttons. Consequence: the New Request project-dropdown scoping cannot be visually verified via UI (verified via backend + verified via the Project Request Center project filter which uses the SAME shared ProjectSelect data source, so scoping IS still proven).

action_items: MEDIUM: Reconcile frontend RBAC for the 'New Request' create-buttons on Project Request Center so custom role manager_o_p (is_pm_scoped) sees the create-request buttons the backend already permits. Same gate likely hides the 'New Issue/Allocation' button on Material Allocations for read-only roles — but per review context that one is EXPECTED (RBAC says manager_o_p has NO write on material_allocations); Material Allocations 'Issue' button IS actually visible in this run and its project dropdown scopes correctly, so that path is fine.
critical_code_review_comments: Shared ProjectSelect (MasterSelect.jsx) is now the single source of truth for project dropdowns and correctly consumes the scoped GET /api/projects — confirmed by all three verified dropdowns yielding identical MOP-scoped output.

scope.py / pm_scope.is_pm_scoped() implementation cleanly extends canonical PM scoping to custom roles (manager_o_p / manager_op / project_manager / project_coordinator). Backend behaviour is consistent across projects, cost-centers, project-requests, allocations endpoints.
Minor: Cost Centers page renders a native <select> (options for PRJ list) while other dialogs mix native selects and shadcn comboboxes — inconsistency across the app, not a functional bug.
